subject.title: Feature: Respect userTimezone in memory file timestamps and naming

question: Should bundled `session-memory` artifacts use `agents.defaults.userTimezone` instead of host/TZ local time when naming files and writing `# Session` headers?
rationale: Current source proves the inconsistency, but docs and shipped behavior currently define host-local `session-memory` output while auto-flush already follows `userTimezone`, so changing filenames is a product and compatibility choice.

options.title: Adopt `userTimezone` for memory artifacts
options.body: Reuse existing configured-timezone helpers in `session-memory`, keep the ISO date shape, and update focused regression tests plus docs.

options.title: Keep host-local `session-memory`
options.body: Document the distinction between auto-flush and bundled `session-memory` so the current behavior is explicitly intentional.

options.title: Add a dedicated memory timezone option
options.body: Introduce a new config knob only if maintainers want memory artifacts to diverge from the existing `userTimezone` contract despite added config surface.

recommendation.title: Adopt `userTimezone` for memory artifacts
recommendation.body: Reuse existing configured-timezone helpers in `session-memory`, keep the ISO date shape, and update focused regression tests plus docs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main ownership spans the implicated session-memory, memory-core flush, and docs surfaces, making this the best routing candidate for the product-contract decision.
